g.text: A small, fast model answers narrow questions with probabilities. Your code decides.
# 1. What happened. This is what Jev looks at.
# 2. What we want to know. Three narrow questions, three kinds of answer.
"named_city": Noul(instructions="Did the user say which city they mean?"), # yes/no
"intent": Choice(instructions="What does the user want?", criteria={...}), # pick one
"urgency": Score(instructions="How urgent is the request?", criteria=[...]), # rate
# 4. Jev only observes. Plain Python decides.
Jev on “What's the weather?” (real run, labs/lab6a_jev.py)
Every option gets a probability, not just the winner.
0.08 < 0.5, so plain Python says: ask which city.
Jev: hosted by TypeSafe, via its SDK
Kev: open, same SDK, a local URL
Qwen stand-in: one token + its logprobs
